sub_service: Collection & disposal of solid waste / removal of solid waste from streets and roads
problem_type: Garbage not collected / solid waste not removed from a street or road
department: Sanitation Branch (Health Branch), Municipal Corporation, S.A.S. Nagar (Mohali)
description: Citizens can report uncollected garbage or request removal of solid waste from streets/roads. Mohali's Citizen Charter states three separate figures for this service that should not be conflated: the Citizen Charter's own Service Standard is 2 working days for 'Collection & disposal of Solid Waste'; the Punjab Right to Service Act 2011 sets a statutory 2-day limit for 'Removal of Solid waste from streets/roads' (Service No. 82) with its own designated/appellate chain; and the internal Grievance Redress Mechanism (toll-free/app system) has a 1-day nodal-officer norm.
procedure: Register a complaint via: (1) the Municipal Corporation's toll-free number 1800-137-0007 (operational since December 2013; complaint centre works 9:30 AM-4:00 PM on working days) -- a unique Complaint ID is generated and sent by SMS, and a further SMS confirms resolution; (2) the 'MC CRAMAT' Android mobile app (search on Google Play Store, register with email/mobile/password, then file complaints with photo and category); (3) the Department of Local Government Punjab's state-wide toll-free number 1800-1800-0172; or (4) in person at the Complaint Centre, Municipal Corporation Office, Sector 68, S.A.S. Nagar (working hours 9:00 AM-4:00 PM, excluding public holidays).
required_information: Locality / ward / address of the uncollected garbage
sla: Citizen Charter Service Standard: 2 working days for 'Collection & disposal of Solid Waste' (Section 2.3). Punjab Right to Service Act 2011, Service No. 82 ('Removal of Solid waste from streets/roads'): 2 days, statutory. Grievance Redress Mechanism (Section 3.3, Table-2) nodal-officer norm for Sanitation complaints: 1 day.
expected_resolution_time: 2 days (Citizen Charter service standard and RTS Act statutory limit) / 1 day (internal GRM nodal-officer norm)
complaint_channel: In person: Complaint Centre, Municipal Corporation Office, Sector 68, S.A.S. Nagar
contact_information: Sanitation nodal officer (per Citizen Charter Table-2): Sh. Sukhwinder Singh, A.C.E., mobile 9888201787. General complaint centre toll-free: 1800-137-0007.
escalation_procedure: Two independent escalation paths are stated in this source. (1) Statutory, under the Punjab Right to Service Act 2011 (Service No. 82): Designated Officer Executive Officer/CMC -> First Appellate Authority: Sub Divisional Magistrate (SDM) of the concerned district -> Second Appellate Authority: Deputy Commissioner of the concerned district. (2) Internal Grievance Redress Mechanism escalation ladder for Sanitation/Public Health complaints (Section 3.4, Table 3): Level 1 - Sanitary Inspector (S.I.), 1-day time norm -> Level 2 - Chief Sanitary Inspector (C.S.I.), 1 day -> Level 3 - Medical Officer of Health (M.O.H.), 1 day -> Level 4 - Commissioner, 1 day.
escalation_authority: Statutory (RTS Act 2011): Executive Officer/CMC -> SDM (concerned district) -> Deputy Commissioner (concerned district). Internal GRM ladder: S.I. -> C.S.I. -> M.O.H. -> Commissioner.

sub_service: Application for a new water supply connection
problem_type: Need to apply for a new water supply connection to a property
department: Water Supply & Sewerage Branch (Public Health wing), Municipal Corporation, S.A.S. Nagar (Mohali)
description: Citizens can apply for a new water supply connection. This is a distinct service from reporting a leak/blockage on an existing connection (see WATER_SUPPLY_SEWERAGE_MOHALI). Two figures apply and, unlike some of Mohali's other services, they agree: the Citizen Charter's own Services Standards table states 7 working days for this exact row, and the Punjab Right to Service Act 2011's statutory entry (Service No. 77, 'Sanction of Water supply/Sewerage Connection in Corporation Cities', which covers both water and sewerage connection sanctioning under one combined entry) also states 7 days.
procedure: The source document lists this service in its Services Standards table and its Right to Service Act table, both stating the designated officer and time limit, but does not provide a specific numbered step-by-step application procedure the way it does for complaint registration. Citizens should apply through the Municipal Corporation's Water Supply & Sewerage Branch / Executive Engineer (O&M) office, Sector 68, S.A.S. Nagar.
sla: Citizen Charter Service Standard: 7 working days (Section 2.3, 'New Water Connection' row). Punjab Right to Service Act 2011, Service No. 77 ('Sanction of Water supply/Sewerage Connection in Corporation Cities'): 7 days, statutory -- same figure, covers both water and sewerage connection sanctioning under one combined entry.
complaint_channel: Municipal Corporation's Water Supply & Sewerage Branch / Executive Engineer (O&M) office, Sector 68, S.A.S. Nagar
contact_information: Executive Engineer (O&M), Municipal Corporation, S.A.S. Nagar -- exact phone number not individually listed for this service in the source document. General complaint centre toll-free: 1800-137-0007.
escalation_procedure: Statutory, under the Punjab Right to Service Act 2011 (Service No. 77): Designated Officer Executive Engineer (O&M) of the Municipal Corporation -> First Appellate Authority: SDM of the Sub-Division -> Second Appellate Authority: Deputy Commissioner of the Concerned District. The Citizen Charter's Services Standards table (Section 2.3) separately lists a generic 'Water Supply & Sewerage' responsible-officer chain of Jr. Engineer -> A.C.E. -> C.E. for the whole services row (which covers this service among 8 others), but does not restate the RTS Act's more specific designated-officer chain.
escalation_authority: Statutory (RTS Act 2011, Service No. 77): Executive Engineer (O&M) -> SDM (Sub-Division) -> Deputy Commissioner (Concerned District).

faq.question: How long does a new water connection take in Mohali?
faq.answer: 7 working days, per both the Citizen Charter's own service standard and the Punjab Right to Service Act 2011 (Service No. 77) -- both state the same figure for this service.

faq.question: What documents do I need?
faq.answer: The source document does not itemize a specific document checklist for this service -- it only states the timeline and responsible officer. Confirm exact document requirements with the Water Supply & Sewerage Branch directly.

faq.question: Is there a fee?
faq.answer: The source states generally that 'service recipients are expected to give complete and duly filled documents and the requisite fee (wherever required)' but does not state a specific amount for this service. Confirm the exact fee with the Water Supply & Sewerage Branch directly.

citizen_guidance: This is a statutory Right to Service Act entry (Service No. 77) -- if the 7-day limit is missed, you can appeal to the SDM of your Sub-Division, and then to the Deputy Commissioner.
